title: Company
description: A company page for Star Atlas that reinforces brand quality, operating principles, and trust without relying on generic startup tropes.
heroTitle: The company page should strengthen trust, not distract from the product.
heroSummary: This page frames Star Atlas and ATMTA around principles, operating posture, and quality standards instead of generic company filler. It exists to support credibility and cohesion across the marketing system.
utilityLine: If specific leadership or team details need to be added later, they should be current and intentionally maintained. The template works well without placeholder bios.

heroMedia.label: Company signal
heroMedia.caption: Premium brand trust comes from coherence, restraint, and a visible standard of care.

heroPanel.title: This page explains how the product is being stewarded.
heroPanel.body: It reassures visitors that the brand, roadmap, support, and product shell are being treated as one connected experience rather than isolated surfaces.
bullets: Clearer relationship between company and community

sections.heading: The standards this redesign assumes the company wants to project.

cards.title: Explain the universe without overwhelming it
cards.body: Every page should help visitors understand what matters and what to do next.

cards.title: Make fewer, stronger moments
cards.body: Premium design relies on hierarchy, whitespace, and confidence rather than constant noise.

cards.title: Keep status and freshness signals honest
cards.body: Roadmaps, newsroom content, and UI states should never undermine confidence through neglect.

sections.heading: A cohesive company page helps the rest of the marketing system feel deliberate.
body: Without a coherent company layer, even strong product pages can feel fragmented. This template ties the brand voice, support posture, and roadmap discipline together in one place.
That makes the overall experience feel closer to a premium product ecosystem and less like separate destinations stitched together.
sections.asideTitle: The company story should support the product story.

finalCta.title: Follow the company story back into product and support.
finalCta.text: Move into the roadmap, contact channels, or the homepage experience depending on what you need next.
